cards.front: What must every ECG order identify?
cards.back: Patient, procedure, protocol, ordering provider, and any limitations/prep instructions.
Immediately — perform ahead of routine work.

cards.front: Order conflicts with what the patient says — what do you do?
cards.back: Perform only what is ordered and clarify with the ordering provider.

cards.front: Patient can't walk but has a treadmill order
cards.back: Contact the provider; they may change it to a pharmacologic stress test.

cards.front: Beta blocker was supposed to be held but wasn't
cards.back: Notify the physician before starting the stress test.
In urgent/emergency situations, documented and authenticated per policy.

cards.front: How many patient identifiers are required?
cards.back: At least two (e.g., name and date of birth) — Joint Commission NPSG.01.01.01.

cards.front: Is a room number an identifier?
cards.back: No — never use room or bed number.

cards.front: Best way to ask an alert patient's identity
cards.back: Open-ended: "Please tell me your full name and date of birth."
Use the facility's temporary/trauma identification system.
Privacy and security of protected health information (PHI).
Patient name/ID, date and time of recording.

cards.front: Wrong patient on an ECG — action?
cards.back: Report to supervisor and correct through the official process.

cards.back: Person legally designated to make decisions when the patient lacks capacity.

cards.back: Bend knees, wide base, keep load close, no twisting.

cards.back: Posture/torso placement can change the ECG.

cards.back: Before (short PR, inverted), hidden, or after QRS.

cards.front: First step when you see VT on the monitor
cards.back: Check the patient (responsive? pulse?) and call for help.

cards.back: ST depression in II, III, aVF.

cards.front: Lead V4R is used to detect…

cards.back: Deep symmetric or biphasic T waves in V2–V3 in a pain-free patient → critical proximal LAD stenosis.

cards.front: ST elevation in aVR + diffuse ST depression
cards.back: Left main or multivessel ischemia — report immediately.
Concave ST elevation with J-point notching, young/healthy, no reciprocal change.

Axis −45° or more, qR in aVL, rS in II/III/aVF, QRS < 0.12 s.

cards.front: First thing to do when you enter a patient's room
cards.back: Introduce yourself (name, role), then verify identity with two identifiers.
Listen, explain purpose; if still refusing, do not perform it — notify the nurse/provider and document.

cards.front: Who may interpret for a non-English-speaking patient?
cards.back: A qualified medical interpreter (in person, phone or video) — not minors or untrained relatives except emergencies.
Face them, reduce noise, speak clearly at normal pace, use written instructions.
Interpretation is the physician's role — the doctor will review and discuss results.
Ask the patient to repeat instructions in their own words to confirm understanding.
Explain, drape, expose minimally; place electrodes under the breast, moving tissue with the back of the hand.
Stay calm, listen, acknowledge, apologize for delays, explain next steps; get help if unsafe.

cards.front: Patient becomes pale, sweaty, faint during ECG
cards.back: Stay, lie them down safely, call for help per policy.
Call for help, pulse check ≤ 10 s, start CPR, get AED/defibrillator.
Lock the brakes, then assess how much help is needed.
Acknowledge, Introduce, Duration, Explanation, Thank you.

cards.front: Trap: V1 and V2 swapped or too high
cards.back: V1 = 4th ICS RIGHT sternal border, V2 = 4th ICS LEFT. Find the angle of Louis (2nd rib) and count down. High placement mimics RBBB/septal changes.
V4 = 5th ICS, midclavicular line. In women place it under the breast, not on breast tissue.

cards.front: Trap: RA–LA vs RA–RL vs LA–LL reversal
cards.back: RA–LA: lead I inverted, aVR upright. RA–RL: lead II nearly flat. LA–LL: subtle, lead III inverted, P taller in I than II. RL–LL: almost no change.

cards.front: Trap: AHA vs IEC color codes
cards.back: AHA: RA white, LA black, LL red, RL green ("white on the right, smoke over fire"). IEC: RA red, LA yellow, LL green, RL black.
Tremor: irregular, varies, from muscle tension or cold. 60-cycle: perfectly regular fine fuzz from electrical devices.

cards.front: Trap: Half standard vs double paper speed
cards.back: Gain changes HEIGHT (5 mm pulse = half standard). Paper speed changes WIDTH (50 mm/s doubles widths).
Diagnostic: 0.05 Hz low cut, ≥150 Hz high cut (adults). Monitor filters can distort the ST segment.
RV infarct: move chest leads to the right only. Dextrocardia: right-sided chest leads AND reverse the arm electrodes.
V7–V9 stay on the same horizontal line as V6 (posterior axillary, mid-scapular, paraspinal).
I, II, III are bipolar. aVR, aVL, aVF are augmented unipolar. Lead I + Lead III = Lead II (Einthoven).
Left Axis Deviation (I up, aVF down, II down) vs Left Anterior Descending artery (V1–V4). Read the context.
I SAW LA: Inferior II/III/aVF, Septal V1–V2, Anterior V3–V4, Lateral I/aVL/V5–V6.
RCA → inferior (+ RV, SA/AV nodes). LAD → septal/anterior. Circumflex → lateral. Posterior → mirror changes in V1–V3.

cards.front: Trap: Reciprocal change vs second MI
cards.back: ST depression opposite the injured wall (e.g., aVL in inferior MI) supports STEMI; it is not a second infarct.
ST depression + tall R in V1–V3 → think posterior; confirm with V7–V9.
Pericarditis: diffuse ST elevation + PR depression, no territory, no reciprocal change (except aVR/V1).
Discordant ST-T in LBBB is expected. Concordant changes are worrying.

cards.front: Trap: Septal q vs pathologic Q
cards.back: Small q < 0.04 s in I, aVL, V5–V6 is normal. Pathologic Q ≥ 0.04 s or ≥ 25% of R height.

cards.front: Trap: P pulmonale vs P mitrale
cards.back: Pulmonale (lungs → right atrium): tall, peaked ≥ 2.5 mm. Mitrale (left atrium): wide ≥ 0.12 s, notched.
High K: narrow, tented T in many leads. Hyperacute T: broad, bulky, in one territory.
High K → peaked T; low K → U waves. High Ca → short QT; low Ca → long QT.
RBBB, RVH, posterior MI (also WPW, normal in children). LBBB gives a deep QS in V1.
Women ≥ 1.5 mm, men ≥ 40 ≥ 2 mm, men < 40 ≥ 2.5 mm; all other leads ≥ 1 mm in two contiguous leads.
Bruce stage 1: 1.7 mph, 10%. Modified Bruce adds 1.7 mph at 0% and 5% first. Each stage is 3 minutes.
Systolic rises with work; diastolic stays the same or falls slightly. A falling systolic BP with increasing work is a stop sign.
Symptomatic severe AS = absolute; asymptomatic severe AS = relative. Acute MI within 2 days = absolute.
≥ 1 mm horizontal or downsloping depression ~80 ms after J point. Rapid upsloping is usually normal.
Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors → hold at least 12 hours.
Tight grip overestimates METs and adds artifact.
Absolute indication to stop the test.
Holter records continuously (24–48 h); the button only marks symptoms. Event recorders save when activated (loop recorders also keep pre-event memory).
Time + symptom + activity is what makes the recording useful.
Check the patient first; a loose lead can mimic asystole.
Holter electrodes go over bone (sternum/ribs) to reduce motion artifact.
Standard Holter recorders must stay dry; follow the device instructions for patches.

cards.front: Trap: AF vs MAT vs flutter
cards.back: AF: no P waves, irregularly irregular. MAT: ≥ 3 P shapes, rate > 100. Flutter: regular sawtooth waves.
A regular narrow rhythm at ~150 → hunt for hidden flutter waves.
Mobitz I: PR grows then drops. Mobitz II: PR constant then drops (dangerous). 2:1 cannot be typed from one strip.
Third degree: P waves march through, PR varies randomly, R–R regular.

cards.front: Trap: Sinus arrhythmia vs sinus arrest
cards.back: Arrhythmia: gradual, with breathing. Arrest: abrupt missing beat, pause not a multiple of P–P.

cards.front: Trap: PAC vs PJC vs PVC
cards.back: PAC: early abnormal upright P, narrow QRS. PJC: inverted/absent P. PVC: wide, no P, compensatory pause.

cards.front: Trap: Bigeminy vs trigeminy vs couplet
cards.back: Bigeminy every 2nd beat, trigeminy every 3rd. Couplet = 2 PVCs in a row; 3+ = VT run.

cards.front: Trap: Failure to capture vs failure to sense
cards.back: Capture: spike, no response. Sense: spikes ignore the patient's own beats.

cards.front: Trap: Fine VF vs asystole vs loose lead
cards.back: Confirm in two leads, check gain and connections, CHECK THE PATIENT.
1500 ÷ SMALL boxes, 300 ÷ LARGE boxes — regular rhythms only. Irregular → 6-second × 10.
QT ÷ √RR (RR in seconds). Don't forget the square root.
Scooped ST = effect. New arrhythmias, nausea, visual changes = toxicity.
VF and pulseless VT are shocked. Asystole and PEA are not.
Beta blocker / ACE inhibitor / ARB / dihydropyridine CCB (little AV effect).
